newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks steady, slightly lower in late trading.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks steady, slightly lower in late trading.

text.p: U.S. stocks were hovering at lower levels in late trading Tuesday, buffeted by some profit-taking after the Dow industrials and Standard & Poor's 500 Index both hit new record closing highs on Monday.
The Dow industrials were down about a half percent, losing 15 to 2620, and the Standard & Poor's 500 Index lost five points to 832.
Market breadth was negative, with losing stocks outnumbering gaining stocks 13 to 10 on the New York Stock Exchange.
Tech stocks took it on the chin, with the Nasdaq Composite Index sinking nine points to 1335, losing 0.67 percent.

The index was dragged lower by sharp losses in chipmaker Intel Corp which fell sharply after rival Digital Equipment Corp filed a patent infringement lawsuit against Intel and said it would see a "huge" damage award.
Intel fell 6-1/2 to 152-5/8. Digital rose 1-7/8 to 35.
International Business Machines Corp rose 3-5/8 to a new all-time high of 175-1/2 after Goldman Sachs put Big Blue on its recommended list and said it could reach $200 to $225.
